facts.text: Bingham Lake was platted on July 28 1875 and officially incorporated in 1900, marking its formal establishment as a city.
The city takes its name from the adjacent Bingham Lake, a 270‑acre shallow body that never exceeds 10 feet in depth.
European‑American settlement began in the late 1860s, spurred by the Homestead Act and expanding railroad lines that opened the prairie for farming.
A tile factory operated in Bingham Lake, producing up to 8,000 tiles daily under John Henderson’s management and employing eleven workers.
A post office served the community from 1871 until its closure in 1992, reflecting the town’s long‑standing civic infrastructure.
The town has weathered several tornadoes, including a powerful one on March 29 1998 and additional tornado reports in 2009 and 2019.
